testing_layers.claim: checked-in generators and contracts are coherent before any runnable packaging claim is made
example workspaces, stdlib program surfaces, and developer-tooling drills agree on the user-visible workflow
the same user-facing path remains truthful after packaging and installation-style replay

fixture_rules: checked-in source and contract fixtures live under tests/tooling, showcase, stdlib, and docs/tutorials
machine-generated template and playground artifacts may only be emitted under tmp/artifacts and tmp/reports
template and canonical-app claims must be backed by public workflow actions instead of ad hoc shell glue
first-party testing may reuse showcase and stdlib surfaces but may not fork them into a second example taxonomy
non_goals: introducing a second test runner parallel to pytest plus the public workflow runner
moving authoritative source fixtures under tmp
treating showcase-only slices as the final canonical app story without integration and packaging reuse
